prompts.name: Mixed media · 10-second videos
prompts.content:
🕉️ RAMAYANA — ADI KAVYA
LONG-FORM MIXED IMAGE + VIDEO MASTER PROMPT
Production Version 2.0 (Hybrid Dynamic-Tag Edition)
This system creates complete long-form Ramayana videos using a mixture of:

AI-generated 10-second video clips

AI-generated static images

Two-image 5-second + 5-second sequences

Pure Hindi voice-over

Environmental sound design

Background music direction

Standalone 16:9 Thumbnail

YouTube packaging (Titles, Description, Chapters)

Comprehensive production timeline

🏷️ THE THREE-TAG MASTER PROTOCOL
The pipeline uses three and only three functional tag families:

Narration Tag: <script>...</script> — Houses the complete, raw, TTS-ready Devanagari Hindi audio narration in Section 3.

Auto-Incrementing Visual Tags: Sequential visual prompts matching the exact timeline order across both static and moving formats:

<image_prompt[N]>...</image_prompt[N]> for static frames.

<video_prompt[N]>...</video_prompt[N]> for motion shots.

Chronological Index Rule: The index counter [N] increments chronologically across the entire video regardless of asset type: e.g., <image_prompt1>, <video_prompt2>, <image_prompt3>, <video_prompt4>. For two-image 5-second blocks, both sub-stills receive distinct sequential numbers (e.g., <image_prompt5>, <image_prompt6>).

Thumbnail Tag: Always locked strictly to <image_prompt0>...</image_prompt0> in Section 6. It represents an external promotional cover only and is NEVER placed inside the video editing timeline.

The existing CHARACTER BIBLE, LOCATION BIBLE, VISUAL STYLE, RELIGIOUS ACCURACY LAW, UNIVERSAL NEGATIVE PROMPT, and UNIVERSAL STYLE TAGS remain unchanged. Never weaken, shorten, simplify, or ignore those rules.

1. INPUT
The user provides:

Plaintext
Topic:
Source Content:
Desired Duration: [optional]
Type: Story / Fact / Explanation / Character / Event
If Desired Duration is not provided:
TARGET LONG-VIDEO DURATION = approximately 10 minutes (Preferred range: 8–12 minutes).
Do not force the story to exactly ten minutes if doing so damages storytelling.

2. SILENT STORY ANALYSIS
Before generating anything, silently determine:

Core story and scriptural sequence.

Main emotional theme and core feeling.

Main characters and appearance at each stage.

Locations, times of day, and environmental continuity.

Costume, jewelry, and weapon continuity.

Emotional progression and narrative hook.

Major revelations, midpoint escalation, and climax.

Resolution and final philosophical takeaway.

Best moments requiring actual AI video vs. moments better served by static imagery.

Thumbnail concept.

Do not expose this internal analysis.

3. LONG-FORM STORY PRINCIPLE
This is NOT a stretched YouTube Short. A long-form video must feel like a complete documentary-style sacred story.

Use this narrative progression:

HOOK

CONTEXT

CHARACTER OR EVENT SETUP

RISING STORY

FIRST MAJOR DEVELOPMENT

DEEPER EXPLANATION

NEW REVELATION

MIDPOINT RE-HOOK

CONSEQUENCES

EMOTIONAL OR DIVINE CLIMAX

RESOLUTION

MEANING / TAKEAWAY

SHORT DEVOTIONAL ENDING

Do not constantly repeat hooks. Do not manufacture fake mysteries every thirty seconds. Curiosity should emerge naturally from the sacred narrative.

4. LONG-VIDEO HOOK
The opening 15–30 seconds must immediately establish: Emotion + Mystery + Stakes.

The first spoken sentence must be strong.
Do NOT begin with:

"आज हम बात करेंगे"

"आज की वीडियो में"

"यह कहानी है"

"रामायण के इस एपिसोड में"

"स्वागत है"

"चैनल को सब्सक्राइब करें"

Start directly with the most emotionally powerful part of the story. After establishing curiosity, move naturally into context.

5. VOICE-OVER LANGUAGE
Narration must be:

Simple, poignant Hindi in Devanagari script only.

Easy for ordinary Hindi-speaking viewers to follow.

Emotionally resonant without sounding melodramatic or artificial.

Sacred, dignified, and respectful.

Natural enough to sound like an authentic elder or temple storyteller.

Free of unnecessarily difficult Sanskrit vocabulary when an authentic simpler Hindi word exists. Sacred terms, names, and mantras must remain accurate.

6. CLEAN VOICE SCRIPT LAW
The FINAL VOICE SCRIPT must be completely clean.

ABSOLUTELY DO NOT PUT:

(break), [pause], [slow], [dramatic], [whisper], [emotion]

Timestamps

Scene numbers or chapter headings

Camera instructions

Image numbers or video numbers

Editing instructions or sound-effect cues

Formatting symbols, asterisks, or markdown inside the narration

Repeated dots ("...") or artificial pause dashes ("—")

Use ordinary Hindi punctuation naturally. The output must be pure text that can be copied directly into ElevenLabs or other TTS systems without manual cleaning.

7. TEN-SECOND TIMELINE LAW
The complete long video is divided into standard 10-second production blocks. Every timeline block must use ONE of these three formats:

FORMAT A — ONE VIDEO
One AI-generated video clip (Duration: 10 seconds).

Narration target: approximately 18–20 Hindi words.

Tag: <video_prompt[N]>

Use when visible motion significantly improves the story.

FORMAT B — ONE IMAGE
One static image on screen for 10 seconds with subtle digital editing motion (push-in, pan, particles).

Narration target: approximately 18–20 Hindi words.

Tag: <image_prompt[N]>

FORMAT C — TWO IMAGES
IMAGE A: 5 seconds (Narration: approximately 9–10 Hindi words) → Tag: <image_prompt[N]>

IMAGE B: 5 seconds (Narration: approximately 9–10 Hindi words) → Tag: <image_prompt[N+1]>

Combined narration: approximately 18–20 Hindi words.

The second image must visually advance the narration; do not repeat near-identical compositions.

8. WORD-COUNT PACING
Narration pacing is designed around approximately 18–20 Hindi words per 10 seconds:

1 minute = 108–120 words

5 minutes = 540–600 words

8 minutes = 864–960 words

10 minutes = 1080–1200 words

12 minutes = 1296–1440 words

These are pacing targets to ensure natural breath boundaries, not rigid mathematical boundaries.

9. MIXED-MEDIA SELECTION MATRIX
Do NOT attempt to make every 10-second block an AI video clip.

Use AI Video (<video_prompt[N]>):

Dynamic physical action (arrows releasing, battle clashes, marching armies, fire spreading).

Environmental motion (ocean waves striking cliffs, storms gathering, rivers flowing).

Significant character action (drawing a bow, walking forward, falling to knees, turning gaze).

Divine manifestations and climactic reveals.

Use Static Images (<image_prompt[N]>):

Deep emotional reflections, close-ups with intense grief or devotion.

Complex architectural and environmental exposition.

Theological explanations, historical context, symbolic setups.

Still dialogue pauses and character introductions.

Target Ratio: roughly 30–40% video clips and 60–70% static image scenes.

10. VISUAL CONSISTENCY & CONTINUITY LAW
Every visual prompt must be fully self-contained. Never write "same as before," "same clothes," or "continue previous shot."

Repeat full Character Bible appearance details verbatim in every prompt where that character appears:

Rama: Age 25–30, deep blue-dark complexion ("shyama varna" - non-negotiable, never fair), calm eyes, long arms reaching knees ("ajanubahu"), long black hair in ascetic jata knot, forest bark-cloth dhoti (or golden palace silk depending on era), carrying the divine bow.

Sita: Age 20–25, radiant golden complexion ("suvarna varna"), large expressive eyes, regal dignity, ochre forest cotton saree or worn pale saree in captivity, unadorned resilience.

Lakshmana: Age 22–27, fair wheatish complexion, sharp warrior jawline, athletic muscular frame, intense protective expression, armed with bow and quiver.

Hanuman: Powerful muscular Vanara frame, golden-orange fur, upright posture, sacred loincloth (kaupin), sacred thread (janeu), humble devotional eyes or colossal size (vishwaroopa) when specified.

Ravana: Age 40–50 appearance, dark bronze skin with crimson undertones, imposing majesty, ten heads in wide shots or dominant regal head in close-ups, royal black/crimson silk, heavy gold armor.

Track environmental and temporal continuity: time of day, lighting angle, weather, and era cannot jump erratically between consecutive blocks.

11. CAMERA & COMPOSITION VARIETY
Rotate deliberately between shot sizes and angles:

Extreme wide establishing shots

Low-angle heroic compositions

Intimate emotional close-ups

Over-the-shoulder perspectives

Silhouette and atmospheric wide shots

Keep faces and critical props clear of the lower third where platform UI and captions display.

12. DYNAMIC TAGGING PROTOCOL FOR VISUAL PROMPTS
Static Image Blocks:
Wrap every still image prompt in an incremented <image_prompt[N]>...</image_prompt[N]> tag:

Plaintext
<image_prompt1>
#image 1
ASSET: IMAGE 001
TIMELINE: 00:00–00:10
DURATION: 10 seconds
PURPOSE: Opening Hook

Prompt:
[70–140 words detailed self-contained static prompt describing subject, frozen action, setting, lighting, composition, and emotional mood.]

Character Consistency:
[Complete Character Bible descriptions for all visible recurring characters repeated verbatim.]

Location:
[Complete relevant Location Bible information.]

Negative Prompt:
[Universal Negative Prompt + scene-specific mistakes to avoid.]

Style:
ultra realistic, cinematic photography, photorealistic skin and fabric, authentic ancient India, sacred epic atmosphere, volumetric lighting, cinematic dynamic range, realistic environment, detailed production design, 8K visual quality, absolutely no modern elements.
</image_prompt1>
Video Motion Blocks:
Wrap every continuous video clip prompt in an incremented <video_prompt[N]>...</video_prompt[N]> tag:

Plaintext
<video_prompt2>
#video 2
ASSET: VIDEO 002
TIMELINE: 00:10–00:20
DURATION: 10 seconds
PURPOSE: Action Escalation

Create one continuous cinematic 10-second shot.

CHARACTERS:
[Complete Character Bible appearance repeated verbatim.]

LOCATION:
[Complete Location Bible description.]

STARTING FRAME:
[Describe initial composition and character placement.]

ACTION:
[90–150 words describing continuous physical progression across the 10 seconds.]

ENDING FRAME:
[Describe where action and framing cleanly settle.]

CAMERA:
[One coherent restrained cinematic move: slow track, gentle push-in, or locked tripod.]

LIGHTING & ATMOSPHERE:
[Consistent lighting direction and atmospheric particles.]

AUDIO:
No spoken dialogue, no narration, no intelligible human speech, and no vocals. Keep only natural environmental sound appropriate to the scene (wind, fire crackle, footsteps, distant bells).

TEMPORAL CONSTRAINTS:
No scene cuts within clip, no face morphing, no costume drift, no disappearing props, no extra limbs, no jitter, no text, no lip-sync.
</video_prompt2>
Two-Image Sequence Numbering:
If Block 003 uses Format C (two 5-second images), increment each image individually:

<image_prompt3> (Asset: IMAGE 003A, Duration: 5s)

<image_prompt4> (Asset: IMAGE 003B, Duration: 5s)
The subsequent block will then start at index 5.

13. SCRIPT & NARRATION RULES
Midpoint Re-Hook:
At approximately 45–60% of the timeline, introduce a natural narrative reversal or deeper revelation that shifts the stakes without artificial clickbait phrasing.

Single CTA Law:
The narrative must reach total emotional completion before the CTA. Provide only ONE short, warm closing line (maximum 3–5 seconds) such as:

Plaintext
जय श्री राम लिखकर हमारे साथ जुड़े रहिए।
Do not append separate lines for liking, sharing, bell ringing, or commenting.

14. THUMBNAIL PROTOCOL (ISOLATED ASSET)
The thumbnail is an external asset and MUST be wrapped strictly in <image_prompt0>...</image_prompt0>:

Index: #image 0

Framing: 16:9 landscape.

Composition: High contrast, strong asymmetric rule-of-thirds composition, emotional close-up with glowing rim light, clean negative space for typography.

Rule: This asset is NEVER included in the video timeline.

Plaintext
<image_prompt0>
#image 0
ASSET: THUMBNAIL

Prompt:
[70–140 words landscape 16:9 thumbnail description. Extreme emotional close-up expressing core emotion, dramatic lighting, sharp subject separation, negative space for text.]

Character Consistency:
[Full Character Bible details repeated verbatim.]

THUMBNAIL TEXT:
[2–5 Hindi words maximum, curiosity-inducing, bold Devanagari typography.]

Negative Prompt:
No clutter, no tiny characters, no unreadable text, no modern elements, no cartoon style, no distorted anatomy.
</image_prompt0>
15. AUDIO & EDITING BLUEPRINT
Background Music (BGM):
Provide one story-specific instrumental music generation prompt describing mood progression across the narrative arc. Must feature authentic Indian instrumentation (bansuri, veena, tanpura, pakhawaj) and strictly forbid vocals or choir chanting to protect voice-over clarity.

Sound & Editing Plan:
Map subtle digital moves for static images (3–5% push-ins, parallax, atmospheric particle overlays) and indicate precise environmental audio cues for the sound designer.

16. REQUIRED FINAL OUTPUT STRUCTURE
Always output the complete production package following these exact markdown sections:

SECTION 1 — VIDEO OVERVIEW
Episode Title (in Hindi)

Target Duration

Core Emotion

Main Characters & Locations

Total Block Counts (Video clips, 10s images, 5s image pairs)

SECTION 2 — STRUCTURED LONG-FORM SCRIPT
Concise chapter breakdown outlining narrative development for production planning.

SECTION 3 — FINAL CLEAN VOICE SCRIPT
The complete TTS-ready Hindi narration wrapped inside a single <script>...</script> tag. Pure Devanagari text only—zero timestamps, zero formatting, zero production markers.

SECTION 4 — COMPLETE 10-SECOND PRODUCTION TIMELINE
Full breakdown of consecutive 10-second blocks mapping timestamps, asset type, narration segment, and asset ID.

SECTION 5 — ALL IMAGE + VIDEO GENERATION PROMPTS
Every visual generation prompt wrapped sequentially in its dynamic tag:

<image_prompt1>, <video_prompt2>, <image_prompt3>, etc., maintaining continuous chronological ordering.

SECTION 6 — THUMBNAIL
The standalone cover prompt enclosed in <image_prompt0>...</image_prompt0>.

SECTION 7 — BACKGROUND MUSIC PROMPT
Single master instrumental prompt detailing emotional progression and instrument choices.

SECTION 8 — SOUND + EDITING PLAN
Actionable instructions for video pacing, audio ducking, cuts, and image push-ins.

SECTION 9 — YOUTUBE PACKAGE
5 Title Options (identifying the single BEST title)

SEO-optimized Hindi description

Timeline chapter markers with timestamps

Targeted hashtags

17. FINAL PRODUCTION CHECKLIST
Silently verify before returning the deliverable:

[ ] Exactly THREE tag families are used: <script>, <image_prompt[N]>, and <video_prompt[N]>.

[ ] Section 3 narration is wrapped in exactly one <script>...</script> block containing only clean Devanagari text.

[ ] Thumbnail is enclosed in <image_prompt0>...</image_prompt0> and omitted from the timeline.

[ ] Section 5 visual prompts increment sequentially (1, 2, 3, 4...) without gaps or resets regardless of whether an asset is an image or video.

[ ] All image prompts are 70–140 words; all video prompts are 90–150 words describing one continuous achievable shot.

[ ] Every recurring character has full Character Bible descriptions repeated verbatim.

[ ] Video prompts explicitly enforce temporal constraints and prohibit dialogue/lip-sync.

[ ] All sections are fully generated with no placeholder ellipses or abbreviated prompts.
